method: The page converts between WGS84 latitude and longitude and an Ordnance Survey National Grid reference in two steps. The position is first treated as an ellipsoid height of zero and turned into Earth-centred cartesian coordinates on the WGS84 ellipsoid (a = 6378137 m, b = 6356752.314245 m), then shifted to OSGB36 with the seven-parameter Helmert transformation Ordnance Survey publishes for this purpose (translation -446.448, +125.157, -542.060 m; rotation -0.1502, -0.2470, -0.8421 arc-seconds; scale +20.4894 ppm), and finally projected by Transverse Mercator on the Airy 1830 ellipsoid (a = 6377563.396 m, b = 6356256.909 m) with the true origin at 49 N 2 W, false origin easting 400 000 m and northing -100 000 m, and a central-meridian scale factor of 0.9996012717. The eastings and northings are then named the National Grid way: the 100 km square is found from two letter indices that skip the letter I, and the figures inside the square are truncated, never rounded, at the chosen precision, so a reference always names the south-west corner of its cell. Five figures per ordinate is a 1 m cell, four is 10 m, three is 100 m, two is 1 km, and letters alone name the whole 100 km square. Reading a reference runs the same chain backwards: the letters are decoded to a square origin, the figures to an easting and northing, the inverse Transverse Mercator series with its iterative footpoint latitude recovers OSGB36 latitude and longitude, and the inverse Helmert shift returns WGS84. Both directions reproduce the two worked examples printed in the Ordnance Survey guide: the annexe C.1 projection of 52 39 27.2531 N 1 43 04.5177 E to 651409.903 m east and 313177.270 m north, and the annexe D Helmert transformation of 3790644.900, -110149.210, 5111482.970 m to 3790269.549, -110038.064, 5111050.261 m, which projects to 422297.792 m east and 412878.741 m north in square SE. The Helmert shift is an approximation: Ordnance Survey rates it at about 3.5 m (95%) in Great Britain, so the page says so rather than implying survey accuracy, and OSTN15 remains the precise transformation. A latitude or longitude whose projection falls outside the National Grid, a pair of letters the grid does not define as a square, and a reference without two letters or with unequal or oversized groups of figures are all refused by name instead of being answered. Heights, Ordnance Datum Newlyn, offshore areas and the OSGM15 geoid model are not modelled. Everything runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded, stored or sent anywhere.

sources.title: A Guide to Coordinate Systems in Great Britain (Ordnance Survey, v3.6): the Airy 1830 ellipsoid, the National Grid Transverse Mercator parameters, the seven-parameter WGS84/ETRS89 to OSGB36 Helmert transformation, the National Grid reference convention, and the worked examples in annexes C.1 and D that this page is checked against
EPSG:27700 OSGB36 / British National Grid, the coordinate reference system the page implements, described as Transverse Mercator on Airy 1830 with the same origin and scale factor
Ordnance Survey note in the same guide (section 6.6) that the approximate Helmert transformation should not be used where better than 3.5 m at 95% is required, and that OSGB36 does not exist offshore
